27	/// menu item's nil-target action down the KEY window's responder chain, then the
28	/// key window and its delegate, then the MAIN window's chain — and a titled
29	/// `NSWindow` becomes key AND main, displacing the editor. Measured, with a
30	/// three-mode probe over one ⌘E item whose action lives on the editor's content
31	/// view controller:
32	///
33	/// | second window | key | main | `NSApp.target(forAction:)` | item |
34	/// |---|---|---|---|---|
35	/// | none | Editor | Editor | the content controller | enabled |
36	/// | `NSWindow` | Preview | **Preview** | **NONE** | **disabled** |
37	/// | `NSPanel` | Preview | Editor | the content controller | enabled |
38	///
39	/// So with a plain window every ⌘-item whose action lives on
40	/// `EditorViewController` — ⌘E Export…, ⌘T Split, ⌘0 Zoom to Fit — goes dead
41	/// while the preview is focused, and a panel keeps every one of them alive
42	/// with no forwarding code at all (`NSPanel.canBecomeMain` is false;
43	/// `canBecomeKey` is true, so it still takes ⌘W and the keys below). This is
44	/// the app's first `NSPanel`.
45	///
46	/// **What a panel keeps alive is the items whose action is on the EDITOR's
47	/// own responder chain, and ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z are not those** — which is the whole
48	/// reason this controller is the panel's DELEGATE. Edit ▸ Undo is the bare
49	/// `Selector(("undo:"))` (`AppDelegate+Menus.swift`), resolved down the KEY
50	/// window's chain rather than the main one, and `NSWindow` itself implements
51	/// it (measured: `NSWindow.instancesRespond(to: "undo:")` is true and
52	/// `NSResponder`'s is false), so the search STOPS at this panel and asks the
53	/// panel's own undo manager. Measured against exactly the shape this file
54	/// builds: the editor window's `undoManager` IS the document's — through the
55	/// responder chain, since the editor window has no delegate at all and
56	/// `NSWindowController` implements `windowWillReturnUndoManager:` nowhere
57	/// (both measured) — while an undelegated panel silently mints a second,
58	/// empty one, `panel.validateMenuItem` answers false for ⌘Z, and the item is
59	/// greyed out. That is the worst pairing available with the forwarded keys
60	/// below: the one window a person can edit from would be the one window they
61	/// cannot take it back from. So `windowWillReturnUndoManager` hands back
62	/// `editor?.document?.undoManager` and ⌘Z here undoes the step ⌘Z there
63	/// undoes. The assignment steals nothing — the panel's delegate was nil, and
64	/// `NSWindowController` neither conforms to `NSWindowDelegate` nor implements
65	/// one of its methods (measured, all three), so no AppKit behaviour changes
66	/// with it, and the editor window's `willCloseNotification` observer below is
67	/// a NOTIFICATION on the OTHER window that a delegate on this one cannot
68	/// touch.
69	///
70	/// **And the delegate has to be there before anything ASKS**, which is the
71	/// second ordering hazard in the init below and was measured the same way as

73	/// the first request that FALLS THROUGH, because there is no delegate or
74	/// because it answered nil, mints a manager of the window's own and that one
75	/// is kept for good, the delegate never consulted again. Both halves are
76	/// readings: a panel stripped of its delegate answered with a fresh empty
77	/// manager and putting the delegate straight back did not undo it (installed,
78	/// and answering the document's manager when called by hand, while
79	/// `panel.undoManager` still came back the panel's own), and a bare panel
80	/// whose delegate answered nil once stayed on its own manager after the

84	/// BELOW it.
85	///

87	/// `hidesOnDeactivate` defaults to **true** on `NSPanel` (measured), which

91	/// main might not have been: also measured — with

94	///
95	/// **Retention: the editor holds it, and the document deliberately does NOT.**

100	/// `NSDocument` closed its first window and got a save sheet with one window

105	/// exactly what the frozen-file rule permits an extension to be unable to hold,

107	/// close semantics unchanged. It is not `ExportQueueWindowController`'s

112	/// rather than waiting to be deallocated: a window whose controller has been

138	    private weak var editor: EditorViewController?
139	    private let surface: PreviewSurfaceView
140

143	        surface = PreviewSurfaceView(editor: editor, layer: editor.playback.makePreviewLayer())

145	        let panel = NSPanel(

190	        _ = panel.setFrameAutosaveName(PreviewWindowController.frameAutosaveName)

195	        // the only window from which the keys below can make an edit. It is

199	        panel.delegate = self
200	        syncTitle()
201	
202	        // The deterministic door: the editor's window going away is what ends

211	    /// "Intro — Preview". The document's name is in the title because two open

221	        window?.title = name.map { "\($0) — Preview" } ?? "Preview"
222	    }
223	
224	    @available(*, unavailable)
225	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
226	        fatalError("PreviewWindowController does not support NSCoder")
227	    }
228	
229	    deinit {

233	    /// Shows the panel and puts the surface in first responder, so a bare
234	    /// Space or J/K/L pressed here reaches the transport rather than beeping.

241	
242	    var isShowing: Bool { window?.isVisible ?? false }

244	    @objc private func editorWindowWillClose(_ note: Notification) {
245	        close()
246	    }
247	}

251	/// is what runs — and this window's own is not the document's.

412	/// View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full / Half / Quarter (road map 2's phase 8a) — the
413	/// fraction of the canvas the PLAYER's video composition renders at, and
414	/// nothing else.
415	///
416	/// **What it buys, and what it does not.** The compositor's fragment work is
417	/// per DESTINATION pixel, so Half quarters it and Quarter divides it by
418	/// sixteen; the `AVPlayerLayer` then upsamples what it is handed, which is what
419	/// `.resizeAspect` was already doing to fit the canvas into the pane. Three
420	/// costs are untouched, and they are named here so nobody later reads a
421	/// smaller-than-expected saving as a bug:
422	///
423	/// · **The shadow passes.** `MetalRenderer.shadowSilhouette` allocates its
424	///   mask/blur pair at the RECIPE CANVAS's size (`Compositor.swift`), not at
425	///   the destination's, because the silhouette is drawn in canvas coordinates
426	///   and blurred with a σ derived from canvas pixels. A shadowed layer costs
427	///   exactly what it always did at every quality.
428	/// · **Decoding.** `Playback.finishRebuild` sets
429	///   `AVPlayerItem.preferredMaximumResolution` to the canvas size, and this
430	///   setting deliberately leaves it there: it is the DECODE ceiling, and
431	///   lowering it would degrade the picture by more than the resample the menu
432	///   promises — a paused Half frame is meant to be the Full frame through one
433	///   scaler, not a different frame.
434	/// · **The audio path**, which has no render size at all.
435	///
436	/// **It is the player's alone, by construction rather than by testing.** There
437	/// is exactly one builder of the video composition in the app
438	/// (`CompositionBuilder.build`, from an `AVVideoComposition.Configuration` it
439	/// keeps on `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration`), and it is shared by the
440	/// preview, both export passes and the offline one-frame render. Rather than
441	/// give that function an argument every caller would have to pass correctly,
442	/// `Playback.previewComposition` copies the configuration it was handed,
443	/// overrides `renderSize` on the COPY and builds from that —
444	/// `ExportWriter.videoComposition(_:settings:)`'s shape exactly, which does
445	/// the same to `frameDuration` for the export sheet's frame-rate popup. The
446	/// export and `render_frame` paths are therefore not merely unchanged but
447	/// UNREACHABLE from this setting: they never see the copy.
448	///
449	/// **No MCP mirror is owed and none may be added.** The parity rule (spec §7.9)
450	/// is that every user-visible EDIT gets a tool; this edits nothing, and there
451	/// is nothing an agent could observe if it did — `render_frame` and `export`
452	/// ignore it by the paragraph above. Phase 7e's export queue is the precedent
453	/// for a feature that correctly earns none.
454	enum PreviewQuality: Int, CaseIterable {
455	    case full = 0
456	    case half = 1
457	    case quarter = 2
458	
459	    /// The submenu's rows, in order. The raw value IS the menu tag, so a
460	    /// fourth quality goes at the END of this list.
461	    var title: String {
462	        switch self {
463	        case .full: return "Full"
464	        case .half: return "Half"
465	        case .quarter: return "Quarter"
466	        }
467	    }
468	
469	    /// What the canvas is divided by — the fraction the row's name promises,
470	    /// before the aspect rule below has its say.
471	    var divisor: Int {
472	        switch self {
473	        case .full: return 1
474	        case .half: return 2
475	        case .quarter: return 4
476	        }
477	    }
478	
479	    /// View state, so `UserDefaults` and not the project (spec §5.2's last
480	    /// bullet), and pinned by the offscreen harness like every other key the
481	    /// app reads (`tools/proof/harness/main.swift`).
482	    static let defaultsKey = "FrameJobPreviewQuality"
483	
484	    /// What a new `Playback` starts at. An absent key — and a stored number
485	    /// outside the three cases, which is what a downgrade after a future
486	    /// fourth row would leave behind — both read as Full, because Full is the
487	    /// only value that cannot surprise somebody who does not know the setting
488	    /// exists.
489	    static func stored() -> PreviewQuality {
490	        let defaults = UserDefaults.standard
491	        guard defaults.object(forKey: defaultsKey) != nil,
492	            let quality = PreviewQuality(rawValue: defaults.integer(forKey: defaultsKey))

497	    func store() {
498	        UserDefaults.standard.set(rawValue, forKey: PreviewQuality.defaultsKey)
499	    }

501	    /// The render size for `canvas` at this quality — **always at the canvas's
502	    /// EXACT aspect ratio**, which is the subtle half of this feature.
503	    ///
504	    /// `PreviewCanvasView` maps every mouse point and every drag handle through
505	    /// `AVPlayerLayer.videoRect` under `.resizeAspect` (`videoRectInView`,
506	    /// `canvasScale`, spec §4.2 and §11). `videoRect` is the aspect of the
507	    /// BUFFER the layer is showing, not of the canvas — so a render size whose
508	    /// aspect differs from the canvas's, even slightly, letterboxes inside the
509	    /// layer and moves every handle in the frame. Measured, because it is
510	    /// cheap to measure and expensive to be wrong about: a 640 × 360 timeline
511	    /// rendered at 501 × 333 comes back with `videoRect` at aspect 1.504505
512	    /// where the canvas is 1.777778, and the compositor draws the whole canvas
513	    /// into that box, so the picture is stretched as well.
514	    ///
515	    /// So the size must be an exact multiple of the canvas's REDUCED ratio.
516	    /// With `g = gcd(width, height)`, every exactly-proportional size is
517	    /// `m · (width/g, height/g)` for some whole `m ≤ g`, and this answers with
518	    /// `m = ceil(g / divisor)`:
519	    ///
520	    /// · when `divisor` divides `g` the answer is exactly the fraction the menu
521	    ///   row names — 1920 × 1080 (g = 120) gives 960 × 540 at Half and
522	    ///   480 × 270 at Quarter;
523	    /// · when it does not, `ceil` rounds toward a COARSER preview, never a
524	    ///   finer one, so the picture is never worse than the row asked for —
525	    ///   999 × 666 (g = 333) gives 501 × 334 at Half, which is 0.15 % above
526	    ///   half and exactly 3∶2;
527	    /// · and when the canvas cannot be divided at all — 1001 × 667, whose
528	    ///   dimensions are coprime — `m` clamps to 1 and every row renders at
529	    ///   FULL size. Falling back to Full is the conservative direction: the
530	    ///   setting is a performance affordance, and an editor whose handles
531	    ///   moved when it was switched on would be a defect where a preview that
532	    ///   is merely no faster is a disappointment.
533	    ///
534	    /// The clamp also bounds the answer from below: `m ≥ 1` and `m ≥ g/4`, so
535	    /// the result is never smaller than a quarter of the canvas and never
536	    /// degenerate however odd the canvas is.
537	    ///
538	    /// **Odd dimensions are fine, and that was measured rather than assumed**,
539	    /// because the rule above produces them (501 × 334 above): a custom
540	    /// compositor asked for 501 × 333, 1001 × 667 and 333 × 501 gets a render
541	    /// context and `newPixelBuffer()`s at exactly those sizes with no error,
542	    /// and an `AVPlayerLayer` fed a 304 × 171 composition of a 16∶9 source
543	    /// reports `displayedPixelBuffer` at 304 × 171 and `videoRect` at
544	    /// 1.777778. Nothing here rounds to even numbers, and nothing should:
545	    /// the buffers are 64RGBAHalf with no chroma subsampling to make an odd edge
546	    /// meaningless. (`ExportWriter.encodedSize` rounds down to even for the
547	    /// opposite reason — an ENCODER's requirement, which this path has not
548	    /// got.)
549	    func renderSize(for canvas: CGSize) -> CGSize {
550	        let width = Int(canvas.width.rounded())
551	        let height = Int(canvas.height.rounded())
552	        guard width >= 1, height >= 1 else { return canvas }
553	        let g = PreviewQuality.greatestCommonDivisor(width, height)
554	        // ceil(g / divisor), never below 1 — see the doc: coarser, never finer.
555	        let steps = max(1, (g + divisor - 1) / divisor)
556	        return CGSize(width: width / g * steps, height: height / g * steps)
557	    }
558	
559	    private static func greatestCommonDivisor(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Int {
560	        var a = abs(a)
561	        var b = abs(b)
562	        while b != 0 { (a, b) = (b, a % b) }
563	        return max(a, 1)
564	    }
565	}

## The editor window

| Area | Where | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| Title bar | top | The project name, with canvas size, frame rate and "edited" (while unsaved) as the subtitle, e.g. `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · edited` |
| Toolbar | under the title bar | Transport, timecode, preview zoom, safe-area guides, **Export…** |
| Preview | middle left | The frame under the playhead, at canvas size, letterboxed |
| Inspector | middle right | The Clip, Media, Document, Transcript and Assistant tabs |
| Timeline bar | above the timeline | The selection block, clip buttons, Snap, the level meter, zoom, track size (see [below](#the-timeline-bar)) |
| Timeline | bottom | The ruler, track headers and lanes |

Drag the dividers to resize the panes. The inspector can be 280–440 pt wide
(304 pt to start) and the timeline 140 pt up to 60 % of the window (300 pt to
start). The sizes you drag to are remembered. Dragging the inspector divider
to the edge stops at its minimum width; the only way to hide the inspector is
**View ▸ Hide Inspector** (⌥⌘I), which becomes **Show Inspector** while it is
hidden and is also remembered. The window is at least 900 × 620 pt.

### The toolbar

From left to right:

- **Transport**: Go to Start (Home), Previous Edit Point (↑), Play / Pause
  (Space), Next Edit Point (↓), Go to End (End), and **Loop**. Loop is dimmed
  while off.
- **Timecode**: the playhead's time, then `/` and the duration of what the
  timeline shows. Click the time to type one: it takes `HH:MM:SS:FF`,
  `HH:MM:SS.mmm`, `HH:MM:SS`, `MM:SS`, seconds with a decimal (`83.5`) or a
  bare number of seconds. Press Return to jump there, snapped to a frame.
  Text that is not a time beeps and the field goes back to the playhead's
  time.
- **Preview zoom**: a popup with Fit, 50%, 100% and 200%.
- **Safe**: shows the title-safe and action-safe guides (90 % and 80 %
  rectangles) on the preview. Remembered between launches.
- **Export…** (⌘E): see [Export](export.md).

Timecode shows frames by default. The Document tab's **Timecode** popup
(Frames or Milliseconds) changes every readout, the ruler included.

content.content:
### What you'll notice after an edit

- A change that only alters how something looks (a property, a colour, text)
  redraws the frame in place without interrupting playback.
- A change to the timeline's structure (a move, a trim, a new clip) rebuilds
  the player in the background. It keeps your place and keeps playing at the
  same rate. While you drag, the rebuild waits until you pause briefly.
- If a rebuild fails, an error is shown and the previous version keeps
  playing.

*Agents:* `set_playhead {t}` moves the playhead and seeks the preview.
`get_project` reports the playhead, selection and in/out range along with the
project. `render_frame` writes the frame at a time as a PNG.

# Canvas, layers, text and shapes

The preview canvas is where you place a clip's picture. Select a layer on it,
then drag to move, scale, rotate or crop it. The Clip tab's **Picture**
sub-tab holds the same placement as numbers, along with opacity, blend modes,
shadows, filters and the effects that hide or highlight part of a frame. This
page also covers what you can put on the canvas besides footage: text clips,
shape clips, image clips, background plates, and matte tracks, which cut the
track behind them.

Every clip that draws can be edited the same way: video, image, still, text,
shape, graphic and nest. A track never holds just one kind of clip. Tracks
stack back to front, and a track higher in the timeline draws in front.

## The canvas

The canvas shows the composition at the playhead, at the project's size,
centred in the preview pane. Under it is a small caption with the canvas size
and frame rate, for example `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps`. You set the canvas size,
rate and background colour on the Document tab (see
[Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)).

### Zoom and pan

| Do this | To |
|---|---|
| Toolbar zoom popup: **Fit**, **50%**, **100%**, **200%** | Pick a zoom stop |
| **View ▸ Zoom In** (⌘+ or ⌘=), **View ▸ Zoom Out** (⌘-) | Step through the same four stops |
| **View ▸ Zoom to Fit** (⌘0) | Go back to Fit |
| Pinch on the trackpad, or ⌥-scroll / ⌘-scroll | Step through the stops |
| Hold Space and drag, or scroll | Pan, when the zoomed canvas is bigger than the pane |

A Space tap that does not pan still plays and pauses as usual.

**View ▸ Preview Window** (⇧⌘P) opens a second window with the same picture
and no handles, for a second display.

### Selecting

- Click a layer to select the topmost visible clip under the pointer at the
  playhead. Hit-testing follows the layer's rotation.
- ⇧-click adds a clip to the selection or removes it.
- Click empty canvas to clear the selection.
- Clips on hidden tracks are not drawn, so you can't click them. Clips on
  locked tracks are drawn but can't be selected or moved on the canvas.
- A clip on a matte track can be selected and dragged like any other clip
  inside its own box, even though it draws nothing there (see
  [Matte tracks](#matte-tracks)). Because it is topmost inside that box, a
  click there selects the matte clip. To select the clip it cuts, click
  outside the matte clip's box, or use the timeline.

The selected clips get an outline. The front-most selected clip also gets
handles.

### Move, scale and rotate

| Gesture | What it does |
|---|---|
| Drag inside the box | Move. Every selected clip moves by the same amount |
| ← → ↑ ↓ (canvas focused) | Nudge the selection 1 canvas pixel |

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

### What you'll notice after an edit

- A change that only alters how something looks (a property, a colour, text)
  redraws the frame in place without interrupting playback.
- A change to the timeline's structure (a move, a trim, a new clip) rebuilds
  the player in the background. It keeps your place and keeps playing at the
  same rate. While you drag, the rebuild waits until you pause briefly.
- If a rebuild fails, an error is shown and the previous version keeps
  playing.

*Agents:* `set_playhead {t}` moves the playhead and seeks the preview.
`get_project` reports the playhead, selection and in/out range along with the
project. `render_frame` writes the frame at a time as a PNG.

# Canvas, layers, text and shapes

The preview canvas is where you place a clip's picture. Select a layer on it,
then drag to move, scale, rotate or crop it. The Clip tab's **Picture**
sub-tab holds the same placement as numbers, along with opacity, blend modes,
shadows, filters and the effects that hide or highlight part of a frame. This
page also covers what you can put on the canvas besides footage: text clips,
shape clips, image clips, background plates, and matte tracks, which cut the
track behind them.

Every clip that draws can be edited the same way: video, image, still, text,
shape, graphic and nest. A track never holds just one kind of clip. Tracks
stack back to front, and a track higher in the timeline draws in front.

## The canvas

The canvas shows the composition at the playhead, at the project's size,
centred in the preview pane. Under it is a small caption with the canvas size
and frame rate, for example `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps`. You set the canvas size,
rate and background colour on the Document tab (see
[Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)).

### Zoom and pan

| Do this | To |
|---|---|
| Toolbar zoom popup: **Fit**, **50%**, **100%**, **200%** | Pick a zoom stop |
| **View ▸ Zoom In** (⌘+ or ⌘=), **View ▸ Zoom Out** (⌘-) | Step through the same four stops |
| **View ▸ Zoom to Fit** (⌘0) | Go back to Fit |
| Pinch on the trackpad, or ⌥-scroll / ⌘-scroll | Step through the stops |
| Hold Space and drag, or scroll | Pan, when the zoomed canvas is bigger than the pane |

A Space tap that does not pan still plays and pauses as usual.

**View ▸ Preview Window** (⇧⌘P) opens a second window with the same picture
and no handles, for a second display.

### Selecting

- Click a layer to select the topmost visible clip under the pointer at the
  playhead. Hit-testing follows the layer's rotation.
- ⇧-click adds a clip to the selection or removes it.
- Click empty canvas to clear the selection.
- Clips on hidden tracks are not drawn, so you can't click them. Clips on
  locked tracks are drawn but can't be selected or moved on the canvas.
- A clip on a matte track can be selected and dragged like any other clip
  inside its own box, even though it draws nothing there (see
  [Matte tracks](#matte-tracks)). Because it is topmost inside that box, a
  click there selects the matte clip. To select the clip it cuts, click
  outside the matte clip's box, or use the timeline.

The selected clips get an outline. The front-most selected clip also gets
handles.

### Move, scale and rotate

| Gesture | What it does |
|---|---|
| Drag inside the box | Move. Every selected clip moves by the same amount |
| ← → ↑ ↓ (canvas focused) | Nudge the selection 1 canvas pixel |

- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

---
title: "The in/out range"
description: Mark a span of the timeline with I and O, so Loop, deletes, exports and other commands work on that passage alone.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The in/out range marks one passage of the timeline. Set it when you want to loop a section, cut it out, export it on its own, or point another command at it.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Mark ▸ Set In', 'Mark ▸ Set Out', 'Mark ▸ Clear Range']}
  keys={['I', 'O', '⌥X']}
  where="Shaded across the timeline's ruler and lanes"
  tools="set_range"
/>

## Set In

Move the playhead to where the passage starts and press <kbd>I</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set In**. With no range yet, the out point goes to the end of the timeline, so the range runs from the playhead to the end.

## Set Out

Move the playhead to where the passage ends and press <kbd>O</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set Out**. With no range yet, the in point goes to the start of the timeline.

<kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> are bare keys, so the menu shows no shortcut beside them, and they don't fire while you're typing in a field. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).

## Clear Range

Press <kbd>⌥X</kbd> or choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range**. The item is available only while a range is set.

## What the range is

The range is a span shaded across the ruler and the lanes. It changes nothing by itself. These commands read it:

| Command | What it does with the range |
| --- | --- |
| [Loop](/timeline/loop/) | Plays the range over and over, instead of the whole timeline. |
| <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | With no clip selected, [Lift or Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/) the range. With nothing selected and no range, they beep. |
| [Speed ramp presets](/speed/make-a-ramp/) | Cover the range when it lies entirely inside the clip. |
| [**Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**](/color/adjustment-clips/) | Covers the range. With no range it covers the selected clips, or the whole timeline. |
| [Export](/export/range/) | Writes only the range when you set **Range:** to **In/out range**. |
| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | Changes the speed of everything in the range. |
| [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) | Opens a new project made of the range. |
| [Transcribe](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/) | Offers **In/out range** under **From**, which takes every clip that overlaps the range, whole. |
| [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Works over the range. With no range it works over the selected angle clips. |

Two other things set the range for you. Selecting words in the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/) makes them the range, and **Preview** for a [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) sets the range to the clip and turns Loop on. Both stay until you clear them.

## Crossing points

Setting an in point after the out point moves the out point to match, and setting an out point before the in point moves the in point. Both points then sit on the playhead, which is a range of no length, until you set the other end.

A range of no length isn't shaded, and Loop plays the whole timeline. <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> treat it as no range at all, and the export sheet doesn't offer it. **Mark ▸ Clear Range** still clears it.

## The range isn't saved

The range belongs to the window you're working in, not to the project:

- Setting or clearing it isn't an undo step, and it doesn't mark the project as edited.
- It isn't saved, so a project always opens with no range.
- It clears when you enter or leave a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/), because a nest's time counts from its own start.

## Good to know

- Edits don't move the range. It stays at the same times while the clips under it change. After <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> on a range, the range is still there and now covers what moved up into it, so a second <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> cuts again. Cutting words in the Transcript tab is the exception, and clears the range.
- Inside a nest you can set a range for Loop, deleting and **Retime Range**, but not for an export. The export sheet's **Range:** stays on **Whole project**, and its tooltip explains that the range belongs to the nest. **New Project from Range** is off while a nest is open.

## With an agent

`set_range` sets either end or both, and clears the range when called with neither. Unlike Set In and Set Out, it won't move the other point for you: Frame Job turns down an end at or before the start. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).

## Related

- [Loop playback](/timeline/loop/)
- [Export a range](/export/range/)
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)

---
title: "Clip names and labels"
description: Give a clip its own name, clear it again, and mark clips with a colour label so a busy timeline is easier to read.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A name says what a clip is, and a colour label sorts it. Both help you find your way around a busy timeline.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Rename…', 'Clip ▸ Label']}
  keys="⇧⌘R"
  where={['Double-click a clip on the timeline', 'The name field at the top of the Clip tab']}
  tools="set_clip"
/>

## Rename a clip

<Steps>

1. Double-click the clip on the timeline, or select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> (**Clip ▸ Rename…**). A field opens over its name strip, showing the name the strip shows. With **Clip ▸ Rename…**, the timeline scrolls the clip into view first if it needs to.

2. Type the name.

3. Press Return or Tab, or click elsewhere.

</Steps>

The new name is its own undo step, **Rename Clip**, even when the click that ended it also made an edit.

<kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name, with no undo step. Saving an empty field or an unchanged name does nothing, so a field you opened by accident is harmless.

**Clip ▸ Rename…** is available when something is selected. With several clips selected, it opens the field on the first of them in timeline order. Spaces at either end of a name are trimmed.

Double-clicking a nest clip opens the nest instead of renaming it. To rename a nest clip, select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>, or use the name field in the [Clip tab](#clear-a-name).

## What a clip shows with no name

A clip with no name of its own shows what it holds:

| Clip | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| A nest | The nest's name |
| A clip from a file | The file's name |
| Text | Its words, or `Text` when it has none |
| A shape | The kind of shape |
| A graphic | `Graphic` |
| An adjustment clip | `Adjustment` |

## Clear a name

The name field at the top of the [Clip tab](/getting-started/inspector/) names one clip. Empty it to clear the clip's name and go back to what the clip holds. This is the only place you can clear a name, because the field on the timeline ignores an empty name.

The field also renames the clip when you type in it, and either way it's one undo step, **Rename Clip**. It appears only with a single clip selected. With several selected, the header reads how many, for example "3 clips selected".

## Colour labels

<Steps>

1. Select the clips.

2. Choose a colour from **Clip ▸ Label**: **Red**, **Orange**, **Yellow**, **Green**, **Blue** or **Purple**. Choose **None** to remove a label.

</Steps>

A label applies to every selected clip as one undo step, **Label Clip**. Labels are for your own sorting, and they don't change how a clip plays or exports.

A labelled clip has a small dot in its colour at the right end of its name strip. On a clip too narrow to fit both, the strip keeps its kind icon and drops the dot. See [Reading a clip](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).

The menu is available when something is selected. It checks a colour when every selected clip has that label, and **None** when none has a label. Choosing a label every selected clip already has beeps and changes nothing.

The [Clip tab](/getting-started/inspector/)'s header shows the dot at the end of the name line when every selected clip has the same label. There's no dot when they differ or none has one.

## Good to know

- A clip on a locked track can still be renamed, because a lock protects a clip's place on the timeline, and a name isn't placement.
- Split, duplicate, detach and paste carry a clip's name and label to the new clip. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) never does.
- The field stays open through a zoom or a change an agent makes. If the clip is deleted while the field is open, the field closes and what you typed is dropped.
- The same field renames [tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/) and [markers](/timeline/markers/).

## With an agent

`set_clip` names or labels several clips in one step, where a person names one at a time. It clears a name or a label as well. It stores any label it's given, and a name outside the six colours draws in the neutral text colour, so keep to the six. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)

---
title: "The preview"
description: What the preview pane shows, what its corner tags mean, and the View menu items that change it.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The preview shows the frame under the playhead, so you can see what you're making while you edit and play.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['View ▸ Safe Areas', 'View ▸ Show Ungraded', 'View ▸ Show Selection', 'View ▸ Show SDR Version', 'View ▸ Show Subjects', 'View ▸ Scopes', 'View ▸ Loudness Meter']}
  keys={['⌃⌘U', '⌃⌘W', '⌃⌘L']}
  where="The editor window, middle left"
/>

## What it shows

The picture appears at the canvas's size, letterboxed in the pane to the left of the inspector. Under it, a small caption gives the canvas size and frame rate, for example `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps`.

The preview is also where you work on the picture: selecting clips, then moving, scaling, rotating and cropping them. That's covered in [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/), and zooming it in [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).

Two settings change how the preview is drawn, and neither touches an export:

- [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) draws it smaller, so heavy projects play more smoothly.
- [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) shows the same picture in a second window, for another display.

## Preview tags

Small tags in the top-left corner of the pane tell you when the picture isn't the plain one. Each shows only while its **View** item is on.

| Tag | Means | View item |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ungraded** | The picture shows no clip's grade. | [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) |
| **Selection** | The picture shows which pixels the selected adjustment clip's qualifier picks. | [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) |
| **SDR Version** | The picture shows the project's SDR version. | [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) |

<Shot
  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
  alt="The preview pane with the Ungraded tag in its top-left corner, the picture with its caption 960 × 540 · 30 fps underneath, and the scopes panel beside it showing a waveform over a vectorscope."
/>

The tags sit in that order, and a hidden tag leaves no space, so **Selection** moves into the corner when **Ungraded** is off. **SDR Version** shows in an SDR project too, where the picture doesn't change.

## Other View items

The **View** menu holds the other switches for the preview. Each has its own page.

| Item | Keys | What it does | Remembered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**Safe Areas**](/canvas/safe-areas/) | | Shows the title-safe and action-safe guides, the same as the toolbar's **Safe** box. Checked when on. | Yes |
| [**Show Ungraded**](/color/show-ungraded/) | <kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd> | Shows the picture as if no clip were graded. | No |
| [**Show Selection**](/color/show-selection/) | | Shows what an adjustment clip's qualifier picks. It needs a selected adjustment clip to turn on. | No |
| [**Show SDR Version**](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) | | Shows an HDR project's SDR version. | No |
| [**Show Subjects**](/framing/show-subjects/) | | Draws the faces, people and salient regions found for the selected clip. | No |
| [**Scopes**](/color/scopes/) | <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> | Shows the scopes panel beside the picture. | No |
| [**Loudness Meter**](/audio/loudness-meter/) | <kbd>⌃⌘L</kbd> | Shows the live loudness column beside the picture. | No |

Remembered means between launches, for every project. The items that aren't remembered start off in each new window, and none of these changes an export.

**View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) sits nearby but doesn't change the picture. It opens the inspector's Assistant tab, beside the preview. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).

## Related

- [A tour of the editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/)
- [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/)
- [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/)
- [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/)

---
title: "Preview Quality"
description: Draw the preview at half or a quarter of the canvas size so a heavy project plays more smoothly, without changing what you export.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Preview Quality draws the preview smaller and scales it back up to fit, so a heavy project plays more smoothly. It never changes an export.

<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Quality" />

## Full, Half, Quarter

Choose **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full**, **Half** or **Quarter**. The menu checks the current choice. The preview redraws straight away, paused or playing.

| Row | Draws the preview at | 1920 × 1080 canvas |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Full** (default) | The canvas size | 1920 × 1080 |
| **Half** | Half the width and height | 960 × 540 |
| **Quarter** | A quarter of the width and height | 480 × 270 |

The choice is remembered between launches, for every project. There's no keyboard shortcut. The [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) shows the same picture, so it draws at the same quality.

## What it changes

Quality only affects the preview. It never changes an export, a [saved frame](/export/save-frame/) or a frame an agent renders.

A lower row saves the work of drawing each pixel of the picture. Decoding your footage, drawing shadows and playing the sound cost the same on every row, so a project held back by those won't speed up as much.

## Good to know

The picture always keeps the canvas's exact shape, so that handles stay in the right place on it. On an awkward canvas size that means a row can draw a little larger than its fraction, never smaller:

| Canvas | Half | Quarter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 999 × 666 | 501 × 334 | 252 × 168 |
| 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 |

A canvas whose sides share no common factor, like 1001 × 667, can't be scaled down evenly, so it draws at full size on every row.

## Related

- [The preview](/timeline/preview/)
- [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)

input.content:
---
title: "The Preview Window"
description: Show the picture in a second window with no handles or guides, on another display or full screen.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Preview Window shows the picture on its own, with no handles or guides over it. Use it to put the picture on a second display while you edit in the main window.

<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Window" keys="⇧⌘P" />

## Open the Preview Window

Press <kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd> or choose **View ▸ Preview Window**. The same key hides it again, and the menu item has a checkmark while it's open. It's always available, even on an empty timeline, where it shows the canvas background.

The window is titled after the project, for example "Intro — Preview", and has a black surround. You can resize it down to 320 × 200, and it can go full screen.

It uses the same player as the main preview, so the two never drift apart. [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection** and **Show SDR Version** all apply to it, but the [corner tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags) don't appear in it.

The window is only for looking. Safe-area guides, zoom and the handles for moving clips stay in the main preview.

## Remembered position

The window remembers its position and size between launches, so it opens where you last left it, on a second display for example. The first time, it opens at 640 × 360 in the middle of the screen. It stays visible when you switch to another app.

It closes with its project window. Whether it's open isn't remembered, so it starts off in each new window.

## Keys

The window doesn't take you away from the editor. While it has the focus:

- Playback keys work: <kbd>Space</kbd>, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd>, <kbd>L</kbd>, the arrows, Home and End.
- The editor's other bare keys work too, such as <kbd>M</kbd> for a marker or <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> for the range.
- Every editor ⌘ command works, so <kbd>⌘E</kbd> opens the export sheet and <kbd>⌘T</kbd> splits.
- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> undoes the project's last step, and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> redoes it, the same steps as in the editor.
- <kbd>⌘W</kbd> closes the Preview Window, not the project.

Bare keys stop while a field in the editor window is being edited, or while the editor has a sheet open.

## Good to know

- There's one saved position for every project. With two projects' Preview Windows open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved to.
- The window isn't listed in the **Window** menu. Use **View ▸ Preview Window** to find it.
- After you save a project under a new name, the title updates the next time you show the window.

## Related

- [The preview](/timeline/preview/)
- [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
